finding.claim: SQL injection in /search via f-string interpolation of the q parameter
finding.sink: app.py:12 db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'")

trace.note: term is read raw from the query string
term is concatenated into SQL inside an f-string with no quoting or escaping
sqlite3 executes the attacker-shaped statement; fetchall() returns whatever rows the injected SELECT selects

finding.guards_checked: None. No parameter binding on this line (the ? placeholder is used in by_owner and product but not here), no quote escaping, no allow-list or length limit on q, no authentication. LIKE wildcards are also unescaped.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:11 reads q raw from request.args with no validation or length limit. app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL string with an f-string and no parameter binding, escaping, or allowlist. There is no authentication or authorization decorator on the route (app.py:9-10). The parameterized queries at app.py:18 and app.py:25 are on other routes and do not apply here.
verdict.reason: The attacker is anonymous: /search has no auth (app.py:9-10), and q flows unmodified from request.args (app.py:11) into an f-string SQL statement (app.py:12) with no binding or escaping, so a quote in q injects arbitrary SELECT clauses such as UNION queries that return other rows.

finding.claim: No authorization on /by-owner or /product/<pid>; any unauthenticated caller can enumerate products by an arbitrary owner value
finding.sink: app.py:25 SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE owner = ? (protected operation: product-to-owner association)

trace.note: owner is read from the query string
query is parameterized (safe from injection) but filters by a caller-chosen owner value
matching products are returned with no check that the caller is that owner

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, session, token, or current-user check anywhere in app.py. The owner column is never compared to an authenticated identity. The SQL is parameterized. Whether this is a flaw depends on whether product-to-owner mapping is meant to be private; the file gives no signal either way.

verdict.guard_found: none. No auth, session, or ownership check exists in app.py (lines 1-26). The query at app.py:25 is parameterized, so it is safe from injection but does not restrict who can query. The owner column is never compared to a caller identity before the rows are returned at app.py:26.
verdict.reason: The trace matches app.py:24-26: an anonymous caller can pass any owner value and receive matching id and name pairs with no check. Whether that is a vulnerability depends on whether product-to-owner mapping is meant to be private, and nothing in app.py (or the other routes, which also expose products without auth) shows that it is, so the candidate's "protected operation" label is an assumption the code does not establish.
